title: What If One Nuke Hit London at 8:49 AM?
description:
What would one nuclear bomb do to London? This simulation puts one 100 kiloton warhead over Westminster and maps it ring by ring, with a second warhead landing in Scotland about a minute before it.

Eight forty-nine on a weekday morning: one hundred kilotons detonate over Westminster, and the first warhead has already hit the Royal Navy's submarine base in Scotland. Then the question: what would the government's three-day household advice mean inside the first hour?

This is a simulation. It has not happened. The facts about the UK deterrent, the Be Ready campaign and the history of the four-minute warning are real and labelled REAL DATA or REAL HISTORY on screen. The strike is labelled SIMULATION: the attacker, the launch point, the yield and the wind are our choices, not a forecast.

Chapters
0:00 Cold open
0:37 The boats on the Clyde
2:03 Four minutes, fourteen days, three days
3:33 The trigger
4:55 Minute by minute
6:34 One warhead, ring by ring
8:03 The day after

Key sources
- UK government, the UK's nuclear deterrent explained: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-uks-nuclear-deterrent-what-you-need-to-know/the-uks-nuclear-deterrent-the-national-endeavour-explained
- SIPRI Yearbook 2026, world nuclear forces: https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/YB26%2008%20World%20Nuclear%20Forces.pdf
- Cabinet Office, Be Ready household preparedness: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/households-encouraged-to-take-small-simple-steps-to-stay-prepared-in-an-emergency
- UK government, what to do in a radiation emergency: https://gov.uk/government/publications/radiation-emergencies-information-for-the-public/what-to-do-in-a-radiation-emergency
- National Archives, Protect and Survive: https://media.nationalarchives.gov.uk/index.php/protect-survive-action-after-warnings/
- ONS, population estimates for England and Wales, mid-2024: https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/populationandmigration/populationestimates/bulletins/populationestimatesforenglandandwales/mid2024
- Hansard, written answer on the Greater London war risks study, 1985: https://api.parliament.uk/historic-hansard/written_answers/1985/jan/16/war-risks-study-greater-london
- NUKEMAP, Alex Wellerstein: https://nuclearsecrecy.com/nukemap/
Blast and burn figures: Glasstone and Dolan, The Effects of Nuclear Weapons (1977), calibrated to NUKEMAP.

How this video was made: the narration is AI-generated (Google Text-to-Speech). The strike, its launch point, yield, target and wind are ours, a simulation built from published models and open sources, not a prediction. The rings come from our scenario engine; we count no casualties because no published study supplies a figure for this warhead on this city.
Maps: Natural Earth (public domain), OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) via OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles. Imagery: NASA Blue Marble and Black Marble. Music: generated with Eleven Music.
